english.title: Obtain a material benefit from a foreign intelligence service
english.standardoffencewording:

english.notes:
(i) Prosecution of this offence requires the consent of the Attorney General, section 37 of the National Security Act 2023.
(ii) This offence should be used where an individual has obtained/accepted/retained a material benefit from a foreign intelligence service for themselves. For the offence applicable to a benefit that has not yet been obtained, accepted or retained, but where agreement has been made, see H101430.
(iii) Section 17(3) provides a non-exhaustive list of what constitutes a material benefit. A material benefit may include financial benefits, anything which has the potential to result in a financial benefit, and information. A financial benefit may be money or a gift with a monetary value. This could include, but is not limited to, a beneficial contract or a direct cash payment. Note, however, material benefits may be excluded benefits under section 17(4).
(iv) This offence may apply to conduct outside the UK but will only apply where the material benefit is or was, or is to be, provided in or from the United Kingdom or, the person engaging in the conduct is a UK person or acts for or on behalf of, or holds office under, the Crown, or is in Crown employment (whether or not they engage in the conduct in that capacity), see section 17(6).
(v) It is a defence to show that the person had a reasonable excuse for retaining a benefit (section 17(7)).
(vi) It is also a defence for a person to show that they engaged in the conduct in question in any of the circumstances set out in section 17(8)(a) to (c). These circumstances are: conduct in compliance with a legal obligation under the law of the United Kingdom, excluding obligations under private law; in the case of a person having functions of a public nature under the law of the United Kingdom, conduct for the purposes of those functions; or conduct that is in accordance with, or in relation to, UK-related activities carried out in accordance with an agreement or arrangement. The agreement or arrangement must be one to which either the United Kingdom was a party, or any person acting for or on behalf of, or holding office under, the Crown was (in that capacity) a party.
(vii) Additional powers of entry, search and seizure are provided in Schedule 2 where there are reasonable grounds for suspecting that this offence has been, or is about to be, committed.
